text.p: Former champion Boris Becker entered the upcoming U.S. Open tennis tournament on Thursday, ending speculation that his recent Wimbledon appearance would be his last at a Grand Slam event.
The 29-year-old Becker announced after his quarter-final loss to Pete Sampras last week at the All-England Club that it had been his last appearance at Wimbledon, a tournament he won three times.
Becker said he realised he didn't have "what it takes to go all the way and win a championship like that."
The German, who won the U.S. Open in 1989, will be giving Grand Slam tennis at least one more try next month at Flushing Meadows.

"I'm very glad that Boris will make at least one more appearance at the U.S. Open," said tournament director Jay Snyder. "He has always been one of the most exciting players in the sport and an integral part of U.S. Open history the last 12 years."
Becker has not played in the U.S. Open since 1995, when he lost to Andre Agassi in the semifinals. He missed last year's event due to an injured right wrist.
Entries for this year's U.S. Open, which begins August 25 at the National Tennis Centre, close on Monday.
